newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No duties seen for Russia, Ukraine sunseed exports.
newsitem.headline: No duties seen for Russia, Ukraine sunseed exports.

text.p: Russia and Ukraine have no plans to impose export duties on sunflowerseed at present, Russian farm officials and analysts said on Wednesday.

Rumours of the export duties surfaced recently on European grain markets. Sunsflowerseed is an important cash crop for Russian and Ukrainian farmers, and both countries are a key source of supply for Western European markets.

"There is no such possibility at the moment," said an official in the economics department of Russia's Agriculture Ministry. "We have no intention of doing so at the moment, and as far as I am aware there are no such proposals."
A senior analyst said Ukraine had discussed the possibility of such a step this year but dropped the idea.

"In Ukraine, there had been talk of imposing a 25 percent export duty on sunflowerseeds, but that has come to nothing," said Andrei Sizov, head of the Moscow-based research group SovEcon Ltd. "The proposals were never signed."
Western European traders had said Russia and Ukraine might try to limit sunflowerseed exports after both countries faced domestic shortages in 1996 due to high exports.

In Ukraine, vegetable oil manufacturers had hoped for an export duty to encourage sunseed producers to supply them at the same time as driving down domestic prices, analysts said. But pressure from producers, who prefer to export for hard currency to customers who actually pay on time, held sway.
"Sunseed producers get "live" money for these exports, and often domestic plants can't pay. So they are actively against any such duties," Sizov said.

Kiev is trying alternative methods to secure supplies for vegetable oil processing plants, which have an estimated annual capacity of 2.5 million tonnes. It has set a procurement price of $200 per tonne on sunflowerseed, around 10 percent above domestic prices.
Pressure from the World Trade Organisation to liberalise global trade would also weigh against introducing export duties in either country, analysts said.

Russia produced 2.75 million tonnes of sunseed in 1996, down sharply from a record 4.2 million in 1995. Analysts' forecasts for 1997 vary widely from around 2.5 to 3.2 million tonnes. Up to half of this could be exported, they said.
High sunseed exports from Russia meant it imported major volumes of sunoil and other vegetable oils last year.
Ukraine forecast 1997 output at 2.3 million tonnes from 2.04 million in 1996, although some analysts' forecasts run as high as 2.9 million.
Exports are put no higher than 1.1 million tonnes in 1997/98 (October/September) from an estimated 850,000 in 1996/97, SovEcon forecasts show. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
